about: Machine-readable progress tracker for the hackathon project. It holds the fixed main goal, every requirement from ProblemSet/, the simulator contract, and plan.md's iterations with task status. plan.md and architecture.md hold the reasoning; this file holds ids, links and status.

project.name: Fuel Supply Intelligence & Resilience Platform
project.event: BUP CSE Fest 2026 Hackathon Finals (in association with Poridhi.io)

stack.llm: Claude API with deterministic template fallback
stack.deployment: docker compose; GitHub Actions CI/CD to GHCR

main_goal.rule: Do not change this section. Every iteration, task and scope change must trace back to it.
main_goal.final_challenge: Build an intelligent Fuel Supply Operations Platform that can observe a simulated fuel network, identify emerging risks, recommend or simulate operational decisions, withstand disruptions, and remain observable and usable when components fail.
main_goal.primary_engineering_question: Can the team build, deploy and operate an intelligent system that helps a fuel operations center respond to changing demand, constrained supply, operational disruptions and software failures?
main_goal.motto: Your job is not only to build the system. Your job is to keep it working.
not_the_goal: Highest ML accuracy on its own

status_legend.blocked: Waiting on something; put the reason in notes
status_legend.done: Every done_when item verified and evidence attached
status_legend.dropped: Deliberately not done; put the reason in notes

iteration_process.summary: Each iteration is one phase from plan.md. Work them in dependency order and never skip verification.

steps.name: Select
steps.action: Pick the first iteration whose depends_on are all done (or already in_progress).

steps.name: Grill
steps.action: Run /grill-me on the iteration scope. Record every settled decision in decisions_log.

steps.name: Start
steps.action: Set the iteration and the task being worked on to in_progress.

steps.name: Build
steps.action: Implement the tasks with tests. Follow CLAUDE.md hard rules.

steps.name: Verify
steps.action: Check every done_when item against the running system. Add proof (file paths, PR links, screenshots, metrics) to evidence.

steps.name: Close
steps.action: Set tasks and the iteration to done. Answer any open_questions the iteration resolved.

steps.name: Sync docs
steps.action: If scope or design changed, update plan.md / architecture.md in the same commit, and update progress.

rules: Every task lists the requirement ids it serves; do not add tasks that serve none.
Requirement status is derived: a requirement is met when all tasks in its covered_by are done.
Tasks marked priority could are only started after every must task in iterations P0-P9 is done.
Keep ids stable; never renumber. Add new ids at the end of a list.

requirements.text: Observe the current simulated fuel network
Identify emerging shortages and operational risks
Help operators decide how constrained fuel should be allocated
Expose the reasoning behind important recommendations
Remain observable and usable during application or service failures
Demonstrate measurable system performance under load
Operate entirely against the organizer's simulator; no real fuel infrastructure
Demonstrate the complete loop Observe → Detect → Predict → Decide → Simulate → Act → Monitor → Recover
Judges can interact with and observe a working system
A usable operator-facing application (a notebook alone is not a complete submission); web app recommended
At least one meaningful intelligent capability
Hybrid policy (LP with automatic heuristic fallback)
Reinforcement learning (optional); if used, must be shown to beat a rule-based or heuristic approach
LLMs support the operational system rather than being only a chatbot around the application
Important recommendations are inspectable: why the area is at risk, influencing signals, relevant constraints, expected impact, confidence or uncertainty, alternative actions
Human operators remain able to inspect important decisions
For each crisis, show how the system detects, evaluates, responds, explains and monitors recovery
ML model unavailable → fallback allocation policy
Invalid simulator response → reject input and raise alert
Prediction confidence too low → human review requested
Backend dependency unavailable → retry / cached state / degraded mode
Use clear mechanisms: fallback logic, graceful degradation, retries, timeout handling, health checks, cached state, validation, circuit breakers, rollback
Reproducible way to launch the application (docker compose up or equivalent documented process)
Basic delivery workflow: Source → Build → Test → Package → Deploy → Health Check → Running
Application metrics: request rate, latency, error rate, service availability
System metrics: CPU, memory, resource utilization
Intelligence metrics: prediction error, model confidence, shortage-alert rate, decision frequency, fallback activation
Logs: important actions, integration failures, decision events, recoveries
Expose health of important components (backend API, database, simulator, prediction service, decision engine, p95 latency, error rate) so judges can tell whether the system is healthy
Primary operational data comes from the simulator
Document any external, synthetic or generated data used
Load-test at least one meaningful application path
Report average, p50, p95, p99 latency, throughput, error rate, concurrency, resource usage
Explain the behaviour and limits of the system, not just an arbitrary benchmark
Organizers may inject surprise domain and engineering events during development or judging; the environment may change
All teams integrate with the same BUP Fuel Supply Simulator (published image, unmodified)
Demonstrate clear understanding of the problem and its constraints, and explain the solution effectively

guardrails.text: Operate only against the simulation environment
Do not interact with real fuel infrastructure
Do not execute real purchases or dispatches
Do not use real credentials or private operational systems
Distinguish simulated results from real-world fuel conditions
Preserve human review for consequential simulated decisions

SIMULATION_SPEED.meaning: Wall-clock ticks per second while RUNNING

hard_rules: The simulator is the world, not the brain: it never predicts, optimizes, recommends or decides
REST is the source of truth; SSE is a notification stream, always re-GET after an event
Deterministic: same scenario + seed + actions + injected events gives byte-identical state
Scenario is baked into the image (baseline, no preloaded events) and cannot be switched at runtime
One simulator instance per participant; no central server
Do not modify the simulator source; judges run the published image
/admin/* and /v1/health bypass fault injection; test fault handling on /v1/* only
Only allocations can be written from /v1/*

read_endpoints.notes: status OPEN|OUTAGE, demand_profile, demand_multiplier, capacity, inventory

fields.idempotency_key: string, 1-150 chars, unique unless replaying the identical request
fields.route_id: must exist and match the depot/station pair

idempotency: Same key + same body → existing allocation returned (guide says 201 in §5.4 and 200 in §9; accept both)
Same key + different body → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH (first submission wins)
Cancellation does not free the key

cancel_allocation.notes: PENDING only; refunds depot inventory; 404 ALLOCATION_NOT_FOUND, 409 CANNOT_CANCEL

error_codes.handling: Bug signal; new key for a new request
Resync; reduce or wait for supply

error_codes.meaning: Depot's in-flight + pending this tick over capacity
Bad enum, missing field, quantity ≤ 0, etc.

sse.protocol: ': connected' on connect; 'event: <name>\ndata: <json>' per event; ': keepalive' after 15 s silence
sse.buffer: Per-subscriber queue of 200; a subscriber that falls behind is silently dropped and must reconnect
sse.replay: None (no Last-Event-ID); re-fetch state via REST after reconnect

events.name: allocation.status_changed
events.when: Allocation created / departed / arrived / failed / cancelled

admin_endpoints.purpose: Advance exactly one tick (works while paused); recommended for deterministic tests
Wipe all rows and reload the baked scenario; publishes simulator.notice
Inject crisis event: type, start_tick ≥ 0, duration_ticks > 0, parameters
Inject fault: type, 0 < duration_seconds ≤ 3600, parameters; auto-expires

simulator_contract.event_filter_rule: Empty id or fuel_types lists mean the event applies to all entities of that type

fault_types.effect: Sleeps before every non-admin, non-health request
Adds X-Simulator-Stale: true to /v1/* GET responses

world.supply_pattern: 22 arrivals: 4 initial-burst arrivals at ticks 12-20, then 18 recurring resupplies spaced 64 ticks (~16 h) apart, sized to about one day of regional demand

domain_insights.insight: 1 sim day = 96 ticks; at the default speed of 8 ticks/s a sim day passes in about 12 s of wall-clock time
domain_insights.implication: Decision cycle in milliseconds; LLM async only; demo at SIMULATION_SPEED 1-2; tests via pause + step

domain_insights.insight: Network demand ≈ 95,000 L/day vs depot stock ≈ 252,000 L (about 2.6 days)
domain_insights.implication: Depots are fine in baseline; supply delay/shortfall makes depot stock binding → risk-based rationing

domain_insights.insight: Initial station stock covers about 0.75-1.6 days; capacities ≈ 1-1.3 days of demand
domain_insights.implication: Stockouts on day 1 without action; roughly daily refills per (station, fuel)

domain_insights.insight: Strong, profile-specific hour-of-day factors (0.45-1.55); simulation starts at midnight
domain_insights.implication: Hour-aware forecasting; busy windows drive the first stockouts

domain_insights.insight: Tongi is reachable only from Gazipur; Cox's Bazar only from Patiya
domain_insights.implication: Single points of failure: pre-position stock when a disruption is scheduled; alert when no alternative route exists

domain_insights.insight: Cross-region routes gazipur→karnaphuli and patiya→mirpur (4 ticks, 5,000 L)
DESTINATION_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED checks on-hand inventory only, not in-transit

domain_insights.implication: Binding in bursts; spread shipments across ticks

domain_insights.insight: Events are visible in /v1/events as SCHEDULED before start_tick
shipment_delay and supply_shortfall are one-shot and never undone
domain_insights.implication: Detect by diffing supply arrivals against first-seen values

domain_insights.insight: demand-history returns at most 2000 rows (about 166 ticks)
domain_insights.implication: Mirror history into Postgres every tick

open_questions.question: What happens when an arrival would overflow station capacity (capped, lost or rejected)?
Exact window of DISPATCH_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED ('in-flight + pending from this depot on this tick')
PENDING → IN_TRANSIT timing (example: created 5, departed 6, arrived 8 for transit 2)
Is demand recorded (as unmet) while a station is in OUTAGE?
Does depot_constraint reduce dispatch_capacity_per_tick numerically or only change status?
How are the 22 supply arrivals split across depots and fuels?
Does region demand_factor multiply the profile base demand as assumed?
